metadata.title: PIRLS 2016 User Guide for the International Database
metadata.venue: TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center / IEA

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This user guide documents how to analyze PIRLS 2016 International Database files using the IEA IDB Analyzer, including the structure of student achievement and background questionnaire data. It describes that the database contains student achievement data and multiple background domains (student, home, teacher, school, and curricular background) for 50 countries and 11 benchmarking participants, but it does not specify in the provided text which exact sampling or replicate weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT, BRR/JRR) should be used. Because this is a documentation/user-guide text rather than an empirical analysis paper, the guide’s primary purpose is to enable secondary analysts to reproduce PIRLS 2016 results using the IDB Analyzer software, which is designed to apply the appropriate complex survey design features when computing estimates. Users should consult the companion PIRLS 2016 Methods and Procedures documentation for the rationale and technical details of weighting and variance estimation; the present excerpt does not report specific weight variable names or replicate schemes.

It also does not report a concrete missing-data strategy (e.g., listwise deletion, multiple imputation) because it is not conducting an analysis in the excerpted text. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling are not applicable/not reported in the sense of an applied empirical pipeline.

data.outcome_summary: This PIRLS 2016 User Guide explains how to work with the PIRLS 2016 International Database for secondary analyses, and it is intended to be used alongside the PIRLS 2016 Methods and Procedures documentation. PIRLS assesses reading achievement after four years of schooling and is conducted on a regular 5-year cycle (2001, 2006, 2011, 2016), with PIRLS Literacy 2016 (prePIRLS) for earlier readers and ePIRLS 2016 for online reading skills. The database provides student achievement data plus background information across student, home, teacher, school, and curricular domains for 50 countries and 11 benchmarking participants, with a total of 346,852 students in the database. The guide focuses on database organization, available file types (SPSS/SAS exports, codebooks, almanacs, item information), and basic analysis workflows using the IEA IDB Analyzer software with SPSS and SAS. It does not report empirical predictive model results or performance metrics in the provided excerpt.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a technical user guide/data documentation rather than an empirical study that trains or evaluates machine learning models on PIRLS microdata. As a result, there are no target variables, model metrics, or country-level analytic sample sizes reported in the excerpt, and the extraction cannot populate PV handling or missing-data handling as applied analytic choices. The sparse fields (e.g., no per-country n) reflect that the text is describing the database contents and analysis tools, not presenting an analysis with a defined analytic sample.
